body: Killzone: Liberation is Guerrilla Games' PSP action game, first released in North America on 31 October 2006. Templar returns after the original Killzone, undertaking missions against the Helghast that involve rescuing hostages and gathering intelligence. An elevated viewpoint replaces the earlier first-person perspective, giving the player a clearer view of the surrounding ground and enemy positions. The change suits a handheld with a different control arrangement while keeping the war and its visual identity recognisable. The player reads an encounter from above before deciding how Templar should move through it.

Enemy positions and the shape of the environment become visible together, making movement between useful positions part of the shooting. The player can judge a route before committing to it, then respond when an opponent changes the situation. Mission objectives provide more direction than simply clearing every hostile figure from the screen. A rescue or intelligence task gives a particular place a purpose, encouraging the player to understand how to reach it. The higher camera makes that planning readable, turning a console shooting series into a more compact tactical action format.

Mathijs de Jonge directed the project at Guerrilla. The campaign and multiplayer gave PSP players another way to enter Killzone's setting between the larger console releases. Reviews generally praised the handling and presentation, recognising that the change of viewpoint served the new format rather than reducing it to a smaller copy. A later emulated edition reached PlayStation 4 and PlayStation 5 in 2023. Liberation remains the series' only PSP instalment, showing how a familiar world can support a different kind of play when the camera and controls are designed together for the machine.
